newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina governor calls for teacher raises.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina governor calls for teacher raises.

text.p: North Carolina Gov. Jim Hunt urged lawmakers Tuesday to bring state teacher salaries up to national levels over four years, but offered no specifics on how to pay for the raises.

In his state-of-the-state address, Hunt said the state ranks 42nd in teacher pay. Starting salaries in North Carolina public schools were $21,333 a year while top-qualified teachers with up to 30 years experience earn less than $43,000.

Hunt proposed raising those figures to $25,000 and $53,000 by 2000. He called for paying a bonus of up to $1,000 to teachers whose students exceed certain standards, plus a 12 percent bonus for earning national-board certificaton and a 10 percent bonus for earning a master's degree.
Hunt also urged lawmakers to toughen teacher licensing standards and tenure requirements and to expand the 43-county Smart Start preschool program to all 100 counties within four years.

"Make this commitment to our children's future," the governor said. "Some people say we can't afford this step forward. But the cost of reaching the national average (teacher salary) is just two percent of the total state budget over the next four years. Surely we can afford that."
Hunt also urged lawmakers to keep the state's colleges and universities competitive, expand worker training programs and improve environmental protection.

"And we have a respoinsibility to pay for it without raising taxes," Hunt said. "We cut a billion dollars in taxes over the last four years. We've saved taxpayers money and given them better value for our dollars."
